issues.should_be: The customer email was received on 2026-10-11 and contains no earlier report date; the email itself is the claim report ('I am writing to report an accident').
issues.evidence: Email header: 'Customer email received on 2026-10-11'. No source shows any report on 2026-10-03; the only report date in evidence is 2026-10-11.

The recorded report_date 2026-10-03 is wrong: the email was received on 2026-10-11, 9 calendar days after the 2026-10-02 incident. Article 4.1 requires reporting within 5 days of the incident <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>, so this is a late claim. Article 7.1 states a claim reported after the Article 4.1 deadline must be referred to a Veridia claims handler, and 'a late claim is never refused automatically' — i.e. it must not be paid automatically <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="3" name="contract.pdf"/>. Coverage is fine (C2 collision is in the Policy Schedule), no exclusion applies, and the C2 documents (photos + repair quote) were provided, but the late report triggers mandatory handler referral, so the staged automatic payment (payout €350, assessor no) must not be approved as-is. The handler playbook's commercial-vehicle referral rule does not apply: the email states no third party was involved, so no commercial vehicle exists. (For completeness: had the report been timely, C2 at-fault with licence since 2012 would mean the standard €300 deductible and no assessor since €650 ≤ €1,500 per Articles 5-6 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2-3" name="contract.pdf"/>, but the lateness overrides automatic payment.)
